approachQuestion.prompt:
Shared service window

Two services run every a and b minutes from time zero. Return their first common positive run time if it is at most limit; otherwise return -1.

Example 1: a=12,b=18,limit=40 -> 36.
Example 2: a=12,b=18,limit=35 -> -1.
Example 3: a=1,b=1,limit=1 -> 1.

Constraints and assumptions: 1 <= a,b,limit <= 10^18. All intermediate values must fit signed 64-bit integers; wrapping is forbidden. Return one integer. Choose the best time bound among the offered correct methods, then the least auxiliary storage when time ties.

options.text: Compute g=gcd(a,b) by iterative remainder reduction. Set x=a/g and compare x with floor(limit/b). Multiply x*b only when the comparison permits it.
options.feedback: Common run times are multiples of the least common multiple. Dividing out the shared factor and guarding the product proves both the result and overflow safety.

options.text: Compute a*b in signed 64-bit arithmetic, divide by gcd(a,b), then compare with limit.
options.feedback: For a=b=10^18 and limit=10^18, the answer fits but the intermediate product overflows.

options.text: Try a,2a,3a,... up to limit, using guarded addition. Return the first divisible by b, or -1.
options.feedback: This correctly searches multiples of a without overflow, but can visit vast numbers of candidates avoided by common-divisor reduction.

options.text: Return max(a,b) if it is within limit, otherwise -1.
options.feedback: For a=12,b=18,limit=40 it returns 18 rather than 36; 18 is not divisible by 12.

feedback.reason: Divide before multiplying and prove a threshold check is safe.
details: Find g with iterative remainder reduction on a,b. Set x=a/g. If x>floor(limit/b), return -1; otherwise return x*b.
Divide a by gcd before multiplying by b to obtain the least common multiple. Test x>floor(limit/b) before multiplication; checking overflow only after producing the product is too late.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the revealed method (guarded-lcm). Let m=min(a,b). Choose its tightest standard worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Exact signed 64-bit integer arithmetic, casting before calculations; arithmetic and comparisons cost one unit. No arbitrary-precision operations.
Iterative method, no recursion or hashing, no input copies. Auxiliary space includes all temporary state and buffers, excluding supplied input and returned output.
Include initialization and any copying; no hidden preprocessing or cache.

options.text: O(1 + log m) time, O(1) auxiliary space
O(1 + log m) time, O(1 + log m) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Euclidean reduction dominates a constant-work guarded product.
details: Euclidean reduction takes logarithmically many remainders in the worst case, attained by consecutive Fibonacci inputs. The guard adds constant work. Only a fixed number of words are kept.
Exact signed 64-bit integer arithmetic, casting before calculations; arithmetic and comparisons cost one unit. No arbitrary-precision operations.

“O(1 + log m) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Correct: logarithmic reduction and constant state.
“O(m) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: This is not the tight bound for remainder reduction.
“O(1 + log m) time, O(1 + log m) auxiliary space”: The iterative loop saves no remainder history or recursion stack.
“O(1) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The number of remainder steps grows with m.
